lines.n_hook: Every market reads your copy differently. Lengua Fina is an agent that finds out what each room actually loves — before it rewrites a word.
lines.n_stats: Seventy-six percent of shoppers prefer to buy in their own language. But translating the words isn't enough — the cultural references have to be translated too.
lines.n_copy: Here's real copy, for a real product: dark chocolate from Bocas del Toro. Its hooks are European — a Brussels praline, café au lait, a glass of Port. The rooms: Tokyo, Brussels, and Austin.
lines.n_run: One click. The agent starts asking Qloo what each audience has real affinity for — artists, films, books, brands, places.
lines.n_log: This is a live run. Every reference in the copy is tested against Qloo's taste data, and every replacement must come from what Qloo returned in this very run. The agent cannot invent a reference — grounded, or rejected.
lines.n_verdict: The verdict: three rooms, three different rewrites — each with its taste facts. The exact Qloo entities, and their affinity scores, behind every single swap.
lines.n_honest: And when Qloo has no data on something — like that glass of Port — it's flagged and dropped. Never faked.
lines.n_outro: Lengua Fina. Every reference, traceable to Qloo. Built for the Qloo Agentic Hackathon.
